message.name: SWARM_RANGE_ODOMETRY
message.description: Broadcast by each swarm member at every ranging event: the raw range measurement plus the sender's own odometry sample at that instant. GPS fields are the sender's global position at the same instant, for ground-truth evaluation.
message.field: Timestamp of the ranging event (synchronized time)
MAVLink sysid of the ranged peer. 0 = no range in this message
Measured 3D slant range to target. (NaN/0) when target_sysid is 0
Ground truth: sender GPS latitude (WGS84). INT32_MAX if no fix
Ground truth: sender GPS longitude (WGS84). INT32_MAX if no fix
Ground truth: sender GPS altitude AMSL. NaN if no fix

Sender EKF GNSS-fusion state, meaningful ONLY from a leader (a drone not flying MC Swarm, i.e. the one broadcasting a finite heading above). 0 = unknown / not leading / sender predates this field, 1 = fusing GNSS, 2 = not fusing GNSS. Extension field, so it is excluded from crc_extra and a drone on the older dialect still parses this message; its absence zero-fills to 0 = unknown, never to "GNSS off"

Sender's open-loop excitation-circle offset (SW_CIRC_R), East component of the vector from the circle centre to the sender. Lets a receiver reconstruct the sender's guiding centre and keep its own formation shape term from reading the sender's excitation as formation error. Extension field: absence zero-fills, and (0,0) is exactly the safe default of "not circling", so a leader, an aborted follower, a peer with SW_CIRC_R=0 and a sender on the older dialect all read alike and get no compensation
Sender's circle offset, North component. See circ_off_e
Sender's circle velocity, East. Pairs with circ_off_e so a receiver can dead-reckon the offset forward over message age using its OWN clock, needing no time sync
Sender's circle velocity, North. See circ_vel_e
